updates.text: 1:30 am: setback — Colab disconnected BOT 1 as idle at 12:15 am and the Sept 2023 v3 run was lost at frame 50/72 (my checks skipped that tab for more than 30 min). Fixed: Sept is back in the shared queue at top priority and BOT 1 reconnected and claimed it; all three bots now run a blocking keep-alive cell that also prints progress every 10 minutes, so an idle timeout can no longer happen. BOT 2 is finishing the South River tiles, then the roughness tests.

1:05 am: South River at 10 m scored (94 marks in the box): water-surface error South River +2.8 m (30 m: +4.1), West Brook +0.8 m (30 m: +0.5), Avery Brook MAE 2.5 m, bias +1.8 (30 m: MAE 1.9, bias +0.7). Finer cells help the narrowest valley but leave a consistent ~2 m high bias, so resolution is not the whole story. Next tests queued on the free GPU: Manning roughness x0.7 and x1.3, and a new 'peak of 30-minute snapshots' output to separate real stage from single-step numerical spikes in steep channels. BOT 2 joined the job queue by itself as planned.

10:00 pm: Crossings module (item E) merged and run on July 2023 v3: 348 crossings in the box. Units verified against the USGS service's own data dictionary (ft3/s, mi2, ft, road deck = lidar elevation of the existing deck, ft NAVD88). At 30 m, 23 crossings sit where the grid's channel cell is higher than the road deck — not assessable at that resolution, now flagged; of the 325 assessable, 32 show modelled water above the road deck. Not quotable yet: will be cross-checked on the 10 m South River run. Reviewer findings applied (worker ownership check and crash-proof loop, NaN-safe scoring, crossing coordinates no longer rounded to 100 m, de-duplicated marks on the map).

9:50 pm: Resolution test 1 — Whetstone Brook at 10 m: water-surface error +1.9 m (was +4.7 m at 30 m; 6 marks, all wet). Second GPU (Colab) running South River at 10 m (46 marks); Kaggle 2×T4 joined as a third machine via the new shared job queue (docs/queue/jobs.json + sim/colab/worker.py) and took Dec 2023 v3 statewide. Four parallel agents: culvert overtopping module, ML training-corpus builder, independent code review, docs (merged).

8:40 pm: July 2023 v3 scored. Water now reaches 100% of the 103 surveyed marks (was 4% with the old physics). Water-surface elevation per reach: North Branch Deerfield 0.18 m, West Brook 0.5 m, Avery Brook 1.9 m (bias +0.7), South River +4.1 m, Whetstone +4.7 m — the two narrow steep valleys run high, consistent with the 30 m cell-mean ground sitting above the real channel; a 10 m test is proposed. Two fixes: grid edges are now open boundaries everywhere (the Housatonic piled up 50 m against the July box's south wall), and the WSE metric reads the deepest cell within 60 m instead of the highest wet cell (dated amendment in the protocol). Sept 2023 v3 statewide started 8:28 pm.

8:05 pm: July 2023 with the new physics (v3) finished on the GPU (4.1 h, 131,644 steps); map tiles are being made now and the automatic score against the 103 surveyed marks follows in ~15 min. Item E: added the USGS Massachusetts Stream Crossings Project (365 modelled road–stream crossings with 10–500-yr peak flows, bankfull geometry and road-deck elevation) to docs/network/crossings_ma.json.

4:55 pm: item D done — the road-network layer on /v2/ now uses a real traffic model instead of the 60/40 guess: each flooded road gets a speed from its water depth (Pregnolato 2017 curve; impassable at 30 cm or when depth × speed is dangerous), travel time to the nearest of 175 hospitals is recomputed each frame (cut off = unreachable; amber = 30+ min further than usual), and detour traffic is routed along the real alternative path with capacity by road class. Dec 2023, 3 pm: 320 segments under water → 5 cut off from every hospital, 18 roads over 90% of capacity. 1,697 fire stations and 5,296 NBI bridges/culverts (334 culverts) fetched for the next step. July 2023 v3 at frame 33/96.

3:30 pm: sub-grid channels are in (rivers narrower than a cell now keep their own width and depth inside the cell; tested on a synthetic valley and a Leominster run). The three storms are re-running on this v3 physics: July 2023 west first (~1.5 h), then Sept and Dec statewide. The v2-without-channels July run was stopped: a 26 m pile-up at the river inflow showed exactly why channels were needed.

2:35 pm: v2 physics passed its smoke test (Leominster, 12 h, 1 M cells in 82 s). Now running the three storms on it — July 2023 west first (17 M cells, ~1.5 h), then Sept and Dec statewide — each tiled and scored with the new water-surface-elevation metric. Fixed on the way: SSURGO storage was in cm not mm; solver time step no longer throttled by the open sea.

2:00 pm: engine v2 written after the three reviews — sea only where connected to the edge, no infiltration or drains on rivers/lakes/sea, soil store that fills up (SSURGO storage + 14 days of real antecedent rain), 2.5 M channel cells burnt from NHDPlus bankfull geometry, rivers start a third full, tributaries added to the state-line inflows, Manning by surface, sea held at the Boston tide gauge (compound flooding), q-centred numerics, and velocity/arrival/duration saved per cell and per road. Waiting for the statewide soils grid (with storage + bedrock depth) to finish, then a 12-hour Leominster smoke test before re-running the three storms.

1:05 pm: waiting on two GPU jobs (July 2023 saturated-soil experiment ~2 h; Boston/North/South Shore at 10 m ~1.5 h). Phone layout fixed (☰ button). REMINDER for Mo when home: open a second Colab tab on the same notebook with a GPU and add the HF_TOKEN secret (optionally a Kaggle account too) so runs can be split across two machines.

12:15 pm: July 2023 western Mass published (Run → jul2023 30m) — and it is the first honest miss: of the 103 surveyed river marks, the model puts water near only 4%. The marks sit on river banks in narrow hill-town valleys; the model's rivers carry too little because the soils are allowed to drink too much (the ground was already saturated after weeks of rain) and 30 m cells smear narrow channels. Running a saturated-soil variant now (antecedent 250 mm, soils at 30% capacity) to measure how much of the gap is infiltration. Boston/North/South Shore at 10 m computing alongside.

9:55 am: Sept 11 2023 flash floods published + tiled (Run → sep2023 30m): peak 58 km² under water, 279 streets flooded. Against the 19 dated road-flood reports of that day the model hits 63% — vs 5% at random road points, a 13× lift. July 2023 western Mass now computing (two radar hours are missing from NOAA's archive on July 9; the big rain on July 10 is complete).

8:35 am: Sept 11 2023 flash-flood run at frame 26/72 (peak so far 35 km² under water around 8 pm that night — Leominster/North Attleboro). ~75 min left, then tiles + score; July 2023 western Mass follows automatically, then Boston/North Shore/South Shore at 10 m.

7:50 am: STATEWIDE RUN IS LIVE on /v2/ (Run → dec2023 30m): Dec 18 2023 rain over Districts 3–6 at 30 m, 97 half-hour frames, radar rain overlay, 609 streets and 320 graph segments under water at the peak, 171 roads cut off, 827 carrying detours. Against the 9 dated flood reports of that storm: 44% hit vs 18% at random road points. Sept 2023 flash floods now computing (~2.5 h), then July 2023 western Mass.
6:55 am: statewide Dec 2023 at frame 79/96 (peak was 103 km² under water Monday evening, now draining: 58 km²). About 35 min left, then ~25 min of tiling and scoring → on the v2 map around 8 am.

6:05 am: the whole Massachusetts coast, Jan 4 2018 nor'easter, at 20 m — all 11 tiles computed, tiled and scored. Against 74 surveyed high-water marks: water at 91% of them, mean error 0.48 m, 58% within 50 cm (North Shore: 15 marks, 0.30 m, 73%). Statewide Dec 2023 at frame 51/96, ETA ~7:20 am.

5:50 am: 9 of 11 coast tiles are tiled and in the whole-coast Jan 2018 view; Outer Cape and Buzzards Bay finish in ~5 min. Statewide Dec 2023 at frame 46/96 — 103 km² under water as the rain peaks — about 110 s per frame now, so done around 7:20 am, tiles + validation by ~8 am.

5:00 am: whole-coast Jan 2018 view live on /v2/ (Boston, North Shore, Nantucket tiled; South Shore and Vineyard tiling now, 6 more to go at ~10 min each). Statewide Dec 2023 at frame 12/96, ~85 s per frame → done about 7:05 am ET, then its tiles + validation (~30 min).

Overnight setback: Colab's runtime disconnected for inactivity around 2 am ET and took the statewide Dec 2023 run with it at frame 43 of 96 (8 of 10 remaining coast tiles had already been saved to Hugging Face). Restarted 4:22 am ET on a fresh L4: statewide run alone on the GPU (~75 min) with tiling and validation chained automatically; the last two coast tiles, then tiles + validation for all nine new coast tiles, run alongside. I now poke Colab every 20 minutes.

First real validation: the Boston Jan 2018 run vs 32 USGS surveyed high-water marks — water at 91% of the marks, mean error 0.54 m, 53% within 50 cm, bias −0.07 m, with no calibration at all. The marks are drawn on the v2 map coloured by error (click one). Validation runs automatically for every published run from now on.

Flooded streets now light up on the v2 map: at the Jan 4 2018 peak, 389 Boston streets are under ≥10 cm (Seaport Blvd, Summer St, Northern Ave, Fan Pier — as happened). Ten more coast tiles (North Shore to Nantucket, 20 m) and the statewide Dec 2023 run are computing side by side on the GPU; both should be done by about 2-3 am ET, then tiled.

First GPU coastal run is live on the v2 map: Boston, Jan 4 2018 nor'easter at 20 m (sea held at the Boston gauge, peak 2.94 m NAVD88 — Seaport, Fort Point Channel and Long Wharf go under at 12:30 pm, as they did). Pick it from the Run menu at /v2/. The tile builder works (121 frames in 14 min). Statewide Dec 2023 still computing.

Statewide Dec 2023 run is computing on the GPU (started 10:11 pm ET, ~65 s per half-hour frame, 97 frames → done around 11:55 pm). Rain on the grid: up to 168 mm, 58 mm average. Soil groups cover 57% of cells (the rest is sea or unmapped urban); the Merrimack enters at the NH line with a 951 m³/s peak. The v2 map now has the road layer with cut-off and detour roads, and a methods page.

Stage 3 physics went in tonight: SSURGO soil groups (375,545 soil polygons rasterised to 30 m) now set infiltration per cell, and the Connecticut, Merrimack and Deerfield rivers get their real USGS discharge where they cross into the state. The Dec 2023 statewide run restarted at 9:54 pm ET with all of it (about 75 min).

v2 map (MapLibre, GPU-drawn) is live at /v2/: rivers, the 1,866 USGS surveyed high-water marks (click one for the measured water height), stage chip, and a player that will show the statewide GPU run from Hugging Face as soon as its tiles exist. The dec2023 30 m run is loading its rain now.

Stage 2 restarted: statewide Dec 2023 run at 30 m on the L4 GPU, now with real impervious-surface data (176 NLCD tiles). Side quest done: 1,866 USGS surveyed high-water marks for Massachusetts (Jan 2018, Mar 2018, July 2023, 2010, Irene, Sandy) are in the repo for validation.

First GPU run paused: the land-cover server (MRLC) times out from Colab. Fetching the paved-surface map on the 10 m tiles through GitHub instead (176 tiles to Hugging Face), then the statewide run restarts. Tile maker for the web map (PMTiles per frame) written and tested locally.

GPU engine verified on the L4: CPU and GPU agree to 0.1 mm; 64 million cells step in 225 ms. First statewide GPU run started: Dec 18, 2023 over all of Districts 3-6 as one connected 30 m model (about 44 million cells), from the 10 m elevation on Hugging Face with NLCD paved surfaces. About 1.5 h.
Stage 2 started: GPU self-test and timing on the L4, then the Leominster test run against today's CPU result.

Stage 1 done: 10 m elevation, 10 m drainage, and the full USGS river network (213,719 flowlines) are on Hugging Face. Switched Colab to an L4 GPU (24 GB) with high RAM; starting stage 2, the GPU flood engine. Note: USGS high-water marks download failed (service returned no data); will retry via a different route.
10 m drainage is live on the site: zoom into any town under Now → Where rain goes and the drops switch to the USGS 10 m flow grid (real rivers burned in), streamed from Hugging Face tile by tile.

10 m foundation data is in: elevation for the whole state (176 tiles) and the 10 m drainage from the USGS flow grids (160 tiles, 263 MB, rivers burned in). Copying both to Hugging Face now (about 2.8 GB) so the GPU runtime can read them.

Both Colab data jobs had died: the 10 m drainage job ran out of memory (the Colab machine has 12 GB) and took the elevation pull down with it at tile 101/176. Drainage now reads the USGS rasters in small bands; both restarted and the elevation pull resumes where it stopped.

New map engine test passed on your laptop: MapLibre GL + free OpenFreeMap tiles, whole-state stream network drawn by the GPU at a steady 60 fps (test page at /v2/). This is the foundation for the rebuild in stage 6.

GPU check: the Colab runtime is CPU-only right now (no GPU attached). Plan: finish the two CPU data jobs, copy the 10 m data to Hugging Face, then switch Colab to a GPU runtime and run everything from Hugging Face so no Drive re-mount is needed.
Progress strip added to the site. Stage 1: 10 m elevation pull (about 20 min left) and 10 m drainage from USGS flow grids (about 40 min left) running in Colab.
